The Your task block and its activity checks now open the activity-4 workspace card, directly before the workspace heading, the supplied files and the editor in DOM order, and renders in that order in JS-disabled Chromium at 390 px. This loop did not re-read the checker rules: the pass requirements below rest on that byte-identity with what loops 1 and 2 read, on the current step text, and on the two rejections below. Activity 4 (Raise your own exceptions, #activity-4) still carries the required authoring task in the inventory.py lesson editor (fieldset #exed, goal "author", the only check for step 4). To pass, the learner must write a raise of the supplied custom exception with a non-empty message at the placeholder, then write handler, else and finally blocks aligned with try, each with its module-logger call, including the exception-logging call in the handler. That covers o1, o2 and o3 as construction rather than recognition, which is what the recommendation (a bounded scaffold with the supplied custom exception and provided module logger) asked for. Residual (not blocking this education finding): the step text names the clause keywords and logger method names quite literally, more literally than the reworded functions step; the learner still has to compose the message, the clause order and placement, indentation and each logger call, so it is guided construction rather than pure transcription. Whether to reword toward goals is an SME/authoring choice, not a reopening of this finding. Gating re-verified in JS-enabled Chromium: a fresh load with an #activity-4 fragment is normalised to #activity-1, the locked activity-4 timeline link and a manual #activity-5 hash change leave the learner on activity 1 (or the current activity), and Continue stays hidden; running (programmatically, on the hidden and still-locked activity-4 editor) the untouched starter, and a variant with every placeholder replaced by pass, leaves data-pep-completed=false on the fieldset and on the activity-4 section.
